keyVerseText: And Melchizedek king of Salem brought forth bread and wine: and he was the priest of the most high God.
rootMeaning: The Hebrew noun כֹּהֵן (kôhên) derives from the root כָּהַן (kâhan), which means to officiate or minister in the priestly office. As an active participle, כֹּהֵן literally denotes one who performs priestly duties. This root sense emphasizes the functional role of the individual as one who executes sacred responsibilities, going beyond the English word 'priest' by highlighting the active service and ministering aspect inherent in the term.
usageInScripture: The word כֹּהֵן appears approximately 750 times in the Hebrew Bible, predominantly translated as 'the priest' or 'priests' in various forms. Its usage spans from referring to pagan priests to the high priest and Levitical priests, as well as principal officers and chief rulers who exercise priestly functions. This range in translation and application reveals the term's broad semantic field, encompassing both religious and leadership roles, and occasionally extending to priest-king figures such as Melchizedek and the Messiah.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding כֹּהֵן in its original Hebrew context enriches our comprehension of the priesthood as a divinely appointed office of mediation and leadership. The term's broad application, including to the Messiah as a priest-king, points forward to Christ's unique role as the ultimate high priest who intercedes perfectly for humanity. Recognizing the active, ministerial nature of the כֹּהֵן underscores the call for faithful service and holiness in those who represent God to His people. This deepens the evangelical appreciation for Christ's fulfillment of the priestly office and the believer's participation in a royal priesthood.
keyVerseReflection: Genesis 14:18 introduces Melchizedek as 'the priest of the most high God,' highlighting כֹּהֵן as a title of sacred authority and mediation. In this verse, the word conveys not only Melchizedek's priestly function but also his role as a king-priest figure, prefiguring Christ. The term כֹּהֵן here enriches the understanding of Melchizedek's unique status and points to the ultimate priesthood fulfilled in the Messiah.
